descriptionChirho: The turtledove (Streptopelia turtur), an onomatopoetic name (tor) for a migratory bird used extensively as a sacrificial offering in Levitical law and as a symbol of vulnerability and gentleness. All auto-clusters represent the same single species across inflectional and syntactic variants: indefinite singular (Lev 12:6), plural (Lev 5:7,11; 12:8; 14:22; 15:14,29; Num 6:10), with article (Lev 1:14; 14:30), with conjunction (Gen 15:9; Jer 8:7), and with possessive suffix (Ps 74:19; Song 2:12). Cross-linguistically uniform: Arabic yamamah/yamamatayn (يَمَامَة), German Turteltaube, French tourterelle, Korean sanbidulgi (산비둘기), Spanish tortola, Hindi panduk/fakhtao (पंडुक/फाख्ता). No genuine polysemy exists; all occurrences refer to the same bird in sacrificial, covenantal, or natural-history contexts.
